notes.1a: There were a high number of fully correct statements. The most common error was the incorrect treatment of the fixed overhead.
notes.1b: Most candidates calculated the sales price variance correctly but much fewer were able to calculate the sales volume variance. There were many correct fixed overhead expenditure variance calculations but much fewer correct fixed overhead volume calculations.
notes.1c: There were some fully correct reconciliation statements. There were also a range of errors including treating the calculated variances in the incorrect direction and the omission of the direct materials and direct labour variances.
notes.1d: This was well answered and nearly all candidates gave the required advice and most also provided calculations to support their answer along with a range of appropriate comments.
notes.2a: The statements showing the net cash flows for both models were well prepared with a high number of fully correct statements. Errors included the failure to account for the improvement cost for IM3 when accounting for depreciation and not applying the maximum production capacity when calculating sales for year two.
notes.2b: A high number of candidates stated one advantage with a few being able to state two appropriate advantages.
notes.2c: The net present value calculations were made to a very high standard with most candidates being awarded full marks. There were no common errors.
notes.2d: Nearly all candidates gave the required advice and most supported their decision with a range of appropriate comments.
notes.2e: There were some fully correct calculations with most candidates discounting the improvement cost correctly but fewer were able to account correctly for the net present value of the additional revenue.
notes.general_comments: Performance was very good with question two being the best answered question.
